Build a continuously playable project

CREATE → COMPILE → CONFIGURE → INTEGRATE → EDIT TEST WORLD → RUN → VERIFY → CONTINUE. Create and compile types first, but connect each current-phase runtime feature to its real owner before continuing. A data-only/staged contract must say when its runtime consumer becomes active. Phase pages provide the sequential Editor operations; asset pages provide matching detailed contracts.

The Phase 2 → 3 map and initialization transition

  1. Before Phase 3, finish movement, combat and resources in L_MovementLab using its early automatic player spawn. Preserve that map/course and the early-phase source revision for isolated old-lab checks.
  2. At Phase 3, compile the session/world/bootstrap types, assign DA_GameCatalog and both area definitions, and configure exactly one root plus registered safe spawns/rooms/reverse transitions in each slice.
  3. Reopen BP_GameMode and change Default Pawn Class to None. Remove any placed auto-possessed player in the slices. Wait for session/area/controller/spawn readiness, apply persistent actors, explicitly spawn/initialize/possess one body, then bind UI and allow input.
  4. Reuse the same player and its existing movement/combat setup. Replace the early unconditional BeginPlay setup with the explicit ready-body initialization path; do not keep a late second Health initialization that refills a travel handoff.
  5. Reproduce movement obstacles, BP_TrainingDummy and BP_Hazard in a development section of registered SliceA. Validate current gameplay there. The old unregistered lab is not made a production area by changing its name or skipping missing prerequisites.

Before pressing Play

  1. Open the specified existing map and check its effective GameMode, Game Instance assignment and spawn policy. Save All after configuring Blueprint defaults and placed-instance overrides; a saved data asset alone is not an assigned reference.
  2. Use native blocking collision for floor/obstacles, query-only shapes for interaction/ability/hazard detection, and the documented target response for combat. Keep X/Z plane, Y depth and camera/facing consistent. A noncolliding visual does not replace an actor’s Hurtbox/Trigger/Blocker.
  3. Place fixtures in reachable relationships rather than invented final coordinates: safe spawn outside hazards/transitions, open floor for attacks, a reachable platform for airborne tests, a switch connected by exact ID to its blocker, and arrival outside reverse travel volumes.
  4. For every persistent placement author one stable PersistentId; for spawn/room/area/NPC definitions use the documented identity scope. Duplicating an Actor copies its ID: deliberately assign a distinct ID before testing. Never regenerate IDs in BeginPlay/Construction Script to reset progress.
  5. Record which definitions and instance Details are assigned, expected initial Profile/WorldState values, and whether the case requires a fresh test Profile or revisit. Use isolated test slots/user data for corrupt-save cases, not valuable player saves.
  6. PIE uses normal registered/PlayerStart spawning, not a convenient Play From Here position that skips the intended arrival route. For persistence proof, observe actual save completion and use a fresh Standalone/packaged process; a restarted PIE session alone is not complete packaged proof.

Fixture status and evidence record

Dummy targets, test attacks, consumables, helmet, test enemies, TestPulse/receiver and NPC lines are development/slice fixtures. Reusable production systems are being proved with them; no final equipment catalog, ability catalog, lore or production level layout is approved by placing them. Retain useful regression fixtures as later phases extend the same slices. Remove/replace only with an explicit regression replacement and updated references.

RecordWhat to write
Identity/contextPhase, map/AreaId/RoomId, fixture class and PersistentId where required; build/schema/content version and test date.
ConfigurationAssigned definitions, component/interface setup, instance overrides, collision/query arrangement and safe spawn relationship.
Initial state/actionXP/points/entry IDs/quantities/equipment/world records/Health/mana/stamina/charges/effect values; exact public request or mapped player action.
Expected/observedAccepted or rejected result, changed owner values, callbacks/token count, UI/visual observation and meaningful previous-feature regression.
Cleanup/retentionRestore intentionally broken test data, retain useful slice fixtures, keep stable IDs, clear old body/widget subscriptions and distinguish normal travel from clean recovery.

A phase completion is an integrated result

Compile new and modified assets, assign references, wire the public request to its owner, save the test-world fixture, run success/rejection cases and the selected regressions, then record observed results. UI and PaperZD can be absent without suppressing damage, action legality, persistence or required cleanup. Use the project checklists and the full validation suite; do not repeat every historical test manually on every page.

Incremental integration audit · 07 October 2026

Inspected documentation baseline 383ac235010c3c7d8ab357eb21b7eebd2b87c19f. A GitHub Pages build artifact was recovered and its source-only Git tree verified byte-for-byte against 3a518e71f0a71d9a5ee7e7636d0c08e19b739685 before editing. The related RPG repository returned 404 through the available GitHub connection; no actual game Blueprints, project settings or installed Editor were available to validate here. Historical engine/repository evidence remains historical, not a new runtime verification.

The baseline already documented ownership and many implementation rules. The audit found that generated creation checkpoints deferred assignment, phase pages lacked an explicit existing-consumer/world-edit sequence, and multiple test Data Asset instances had no direct consumers recorded. This update adds all twelve operational workflows, shared attachment/interface/input/view/data assignments, staged-asset dispositions, reverse consumer edits and explicit map transition rules. The initial two-point curve also cannot fund TestRoot plus a specialization and TestActive; Phase 9 explicitly extends the development point budget through real progression rather than refunds or import-time awards. No registered asset identity, phase, Content folder, original roadmap or historical audit is changed.

Current static results: integration verification record · browser checks. Existing historical measurements: 02 October package audit. Static HTML/link/search/generation validation is not Blueprint compilation, PIE, Standalone or packaged gameplay validation.

Approved resource fixture extension · 08 October 2026

Use the same real initialized player and phase-appropriate maps. The F6 Level Blueprint resource trigger is development-only, disabled by default, and does not add production input actions or a new fixture family. The following expected cases are authored in sources/phase-integration.json, not claimed executed in Unreal.

  1. Resource setup/reset: save L_MovementLab, assign DA_PlayerBaseStats=(100,10,0,50,100,5,15), ensure one real ready possessed player and the three-bar HUD. Play fresh: health100, mana50/50, stamina100/100. Invalid/unassigned definition or unready Stats must keep the body unready; restore the assignment and Stop/Play. Every resource case logs setup, operation, expected/actual values and resets original Stats/fixture overrides.
  2. F6 deterministic case with temporary zero regen rates and full pools: call CanAfford(10,20) then GetResourceSnapshot; the query leaves 50/100 unchanged. Call TrySpend(10,20): Success=true, current40/80 and exactly one coherent event. RestoreResources(10,20) returns to50/100. TrySpend(0,0), RestoreResources(0,0) and restore into full pools succeed without a new event. Reset rates and pools after the run.
  3. F6 rejection/atomicity: start50/100 with zero rates. TrySpend(10,101) and TrySpend(51,20) each fail with both currents unchanged. TrySpend(-1,0), RestoreResources(1,-1) and nonfinite cost/amount tests through BFL_GameRules.IsFiniteNumber validation reject both sides. Observe Reason, no event and no partial write. Nonfinite Blueprint fixture behavior must be verified in the installed engine; do not use a numeric string that silently parses to zero as proof. Reset to the original valid definition/inputs and full pools.
  4. Capacity rebuild case: at zero rates spend to20/40. Recalculate temporary max75/125: currents stay20/40 and the maximum snapshot changes. Repeat identical rebuild: no duplicated modifiers/no resource event. Recalculate max10/30: currents10/30; max0/0: currents0/0 and zero safe HUD fills. Invalid/nonfinite rebuilt input must fail without replacing the last valid Stats cache. Restore original complete inputs and refill explicitly to repeat; never use ordinary initialization as a refill command.
  5. Regeneration timing case: restore original rates5/15 and full50/100, spend30/60, record GetGameTimeInSeconds. At two elapsed gameplay seconds expect approximately30/70 (start20/40 plus10/30, capped at max); log actual elapsed and use rate*elapsed with a small declared observation tolerance. Repeat at varied frame times, pause/unpause, zero rates, one full pool and both full. Pause adds nothing; both full disables Resources component Tick; a later spend wakes exactly one update. Reset by restoring original Stats and full pools, not by stacking updates.
  6. Lifecycle/HUD regression: bind HUD twice and initialize Resources twice with the same ready Stats after spending; no duplicate listener or refill. SuspendResources then TrySpend: reject unchanged and no regeneration; resume an alive ready body with a new time origin. Trigger existing lethal hazard: Resources remains suspended and ordinary Phase 2 restart is Stop/Play (no early checkpoint). Destroy/recreate through a fresh Play session, remove HUD and repeat APIs; no stale callback and gameplay still correct. Restore HUD and fixture gate afterward.
  7. Zero-resource action regression: with temporary zero rates drain both pools, then walk, turn, perform variable jumps/coyote/buffer and the existing ground/air basic attacks against BP_TrainingDummy. Behavior remains the Phase 1–2 baseline. No resource input/action gate may block these. Restore rates and pools, disable bRunResourceChecks and save the lab after testing.

Later specialization, ability-cost, equipment/effect, travel and clean-recovery cases remain phase-gated in the linked phase run-now sections. Original audit evidence above describes the pre-resource baseline; the approved addition registers BPC_Resources without renaming existing assets. Resource-specific current browser evidence: resource browser checks (rendering only, not Unreal).

Keep phase and asset instructions synchronized

Edit sources/phase-integration.json for phase recipes, shared contracts and staged dispositions. Edit the current asset manifest only for genuine dependency changes; preserve existing identities/folders/phases and their order; the explicit approved resource addition inserts BPC_Resources after BPC_Stats in Phase 2. Generated integration blocks are maintained by tools/phase_integration.py through the existing manual generator; do not hand-edit their copies.
